me:2011:q15.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 15
me:2011:q15.question: A pipe of 25mm outer diameter carries steam. The heat transfer coefficient between the cylinder and surroundings is 5W /$m^{2}K$. It is proposed to reduce the heat loss from the pipe by adding insulation having a thermal conductivity of 0.05W/mK. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

The outer radius of the pipe is less than the critical radius
Adding the insulation will reduce the heat loss
Adding the insulation will increase the heat loss

primary.subtopicLabel: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: Outer diameter of pipe, $$\begin{aligned} d_{0}&=25 \mathrm{mm}\\ \therefore \text{Radius: }r_{0}&=\frac{d_{0}}{2}=\frac{25}{2}=12.5 \mathrm{mm} \\ h&=5 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \\ k&=0.05 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \end{aligned}$$ Critical radius of insulation, $r_{c}=\frac{k}{h}=\frac{0.05}{5}=0.01 \mathrm{m}=10 \mathrm{mm}$ As $r_{0}>r_{c}$ , then adding the insulation will reduce the heat loss. Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2011:q26.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 26
me:2011:q26.question: A torque T is applied at the free end of a stepped rod of circular cross-sections as shown in the figure. The shear modulus of the material of the rod is G. The expression for d to produce an angular twist $\theta$ at the free end is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Torsion of Shafts
detailed_solution.markdown:
By using torsion equation we have

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{T}{J} &=\frac{\tau}{r}=\frac{G \theta}{L} \\ \therefore \quad \theta &=\frac{T L}{G J} \\ \therefore \quad \theta&=\frac{T\left(\frac{L}{2}\right)}{G\left(\frac{\pi}{32}\right) d^{4}}\left[\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{16}\right] \\ \theta&=\frac{T L}{G\left(\frac{\pi}{32} d^{4}\right)} \times\left(\frac{9}{16}\right) \\ \theta&=\frac{18 T L}{G \pi d^{4}} \\ \text{or}\quad d&=\left(\frac{18 T L}{\pi \theta G}\right)^{1 / 4} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2011:q27.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 27
me:2011:q27.question: Figure shows the schematic for the measurement of velocity of air (density = 1.2kg /$m^{3}$) through a constant-area duct using a pitot tube and a water-tube manometer. The differential head of water (density = 1000 kg/$m^{3}$ ) in the two columns of the manometer is 10mm. Take acceleration due to gravity as 9.8m/$s^{2}$. The velocity of air in m/s is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: Density of air, $\rho_{a}=1.2 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ Density of water, $\rho_{w}=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ Differential head in manometer $$\begin{aligned} h &=10 \mathrm{mm} \text { of water } \\ &=0.10 \mathrm{m} \text { of water } \end{aligned}$$ This reading is the dynamic pressure head. Hence dynamic pressure, $$\begin{aligned} P_{\text {dyn }} &=(\rho g h)_{\text {water }}=\rho_{w} g h \\ &=1000 \times 9.81 \times 0.01=98.1 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text { also } p_{\text {dyn }} &=\left(\frac{1}{2} \rho V^{2}\right)_{\text {air }}=\frac{1}{2} \rho_{\mathrm{a}} V^{2}\\ 98.1 &=\frac{1}{2} \times 1.2 \times V^{2} \\ \text{or }\qquad V^{2} &=163.5\\ V&=12.78 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively $V=\sqrt{2 g h}$ $h=x\left(\frac{\rho_{m}}{\rho}-1\right)$ $x=$reading of differential manometer $=10 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$ $\rho_{m}=$ density of manometric fluid =1000 $\mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ $\rho=$ density of following fluid $=1.2 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ $V=\sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 10 \times 10^{-3}\left(\frac{1000}{1.2}-1\right)}$ $V=12.779 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \approx 12.8 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: Specific enthalpy at turbine inlet, $h_{1}=2800 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}$ Specific enthalpy at turbine $\text { outlet: } \quad h_{2}=1800 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}$ Specific work output by the turbine, $$\begin{aligned} w_{T} &=h_{1}-h_{2} \\ &=2800-1800\\ &=1000\mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$ Networkoutput, $w_{\text {net }}=w_{T}-w_{P}$ Where Pump work $$\begin{aligned} w_{p} &=0 \\ w_{\text {net }} &=w_{T}=1000 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$ Specific steam consumption, $S S C=\frac{3600}{1000} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kWh}$ $=3.6 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kWh}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

me:2011:q37.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 37
me:2011:q37.question:
The ratios of the laminar hydrodynamic boundary layer thickness to thermal boundary layer thickness of flows of two fluids P and Q on a flat plate are $\frac{1}{2}$
and 2 respectively. The Reynolds number based on the plate length for both the flows is $10^{4}$. 
 The Prandtl and Nusselt numbers for P are $\frac{1}{8}$
 and 35 respectively. The Prandtl and Nusselt numbers for Q are respectively

primary.subtopicLabel: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data:

For fluid P

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\delta}{\delta_{t}} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ (\mathrm{Re})_{P} &=1000 \\ (\mathrm{Pr})_{P} &=\frac{1}{8} \\ (\mathrm{Nu})_{P} &=35 \\ (\mathrm{Nu})_{P} &=0.664(\mathrm{Re})_{P}^{0.5}(\mathrm{Pr})_{P}^{0.333} \end{aligned}$$

For fluid Q

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\delta}{\delta_{t}} &=2 \\ (\mathrm{Re})_{a} &=10000 \\ (\mathrm{Pe})_{a} &=? \\ (\mathrm{Nu})_{a} &=? \\ \frac{\delta}{\delta_{t}} &=(\mathrm{Pr})_{a}^{1 / 3} \\ 2 &=(\mathrm{Pr})_{a}^{1 / 3} \\ \text{or} \quad (\mathrm{Pr}) &=(2)^{3}=8 \end{aligned}$$

For laminar boundary layer on a flat plate,

$$\begin{aligned} (P r)_{Q} &=(P r)_{Q}^{0.5}(P r)_{C}^{0.333} \\ \text{Ratio} \quad \frac{(N u)_{P}}{(N u)_{Q}} &=\frac{0.664(R e)_{P}^{0.5}(P r)_{P}^{0.333}}{0.664(R e)_{Q}^{0.5}(P r)_{0}^{0.333}} \\ \frac{(N u)_{P}}{(N u)_{Q}} &=\frac{(R e)_{P}^{0.5}(P r)_{P}^{0.333}}{(R e)_{Q}^{0.5}(P r)_{Q}^{0.333}} \\ \frac{35}{(N u)_{Q}} &=\frac{(10000)^{0.5} \times\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{0.333}}{(10000)^{0.5} \times(8)^{0.333}} \\ \frac{35}{(N u)_{Q}} &=\frac{1}{(8)^{0.333} \times(8)^{0.333}} \\ &=\frac{1}{(8)^{0.666}}=\frac{1}{4} \\ \left(N_{u}\right)_{Q} &=35 \times 4=140 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

me:2011:q39.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 39
me:2011:q39.question: A pump handling a liquid raises its pressure from 1 bar to 30 bar. Take the density of the liquid as 990 $kg/m^{3}$. The isentropic specific work done by the pump in kJ/kg is

me:2011:q40.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 40
me:2011:q40.question: A spherical steel ball of 12mm diameter is initially at 1000K. It is slowly cooled in a surrounding of 300K. The heat transfer coefficient between the steel ball and the surrounding is $5W/m^{2}K$. The thermal conductivity of steel is 20W /mK. The temperature difference between the centre and the surface of the steel ball is
options: Large because conduction resistance is far higher than the convective resistance
Large because conduction resistance is far less than the convective resistance
Small because conduction resistance is far higher than the convective resistance
Small because conduction resistance is far less than the convective resistance

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Fins and Unsteady Heat Transfer
detailed_solution.markdown:
Biot number,

$$\begin{aligned} \text { Bi }&=\frac{\text { Conduction resistance } \frac{l}{k A}}{\text { Convection resistance: } \frac{1}{h A}}=\frac{h l}{k} \\ \text { where } l&=\frac{V}{A}=\frac{\pi}{6} \frac{d^{3}}{\pi d^{2}}=\frac{d}{6}\\ B_{i}&=\frac{h}{k} \frac{d}{6}=\frac{5 \times 0.012}{20 \times 6}=0.0005\\ \end{aligned}$$

If means that the conduction resistance is far less than convective resistance

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

me:2011:q41.question: An ideal Brayton cycle, operating between the pressure limits of 1 bar and 6 bar, has minimum and maximum temperatures of 300K and 1500K. The ratio of specific heats of the working fluid is 1.4. The approximate final temperatures in Kelvin at the end of the compression and expansion processes are respectively

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{array}{ll} p_{1}=1 \text { bar; } & p_{2}=6 \text { bar } \\ T_{1}=300 \mathrm{K} ; & T_{3}=1500 \mathrm{K} \end{array}$$ For process 1-2 $$\begin{aligned} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}\\ \frac{T_{2}}{300} &=\left(\frac{6}{1}\right)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}}=(6)^{0.285}=1.666 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{2} &=300 \times 1.666 \\ &=499.8 \mathrm{K} \\ & \approx 500 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ For process 3-4 $$\begin{aligned} \frac{T_{3}}{T_{4}}&=\left(\frac{p_{3}}{p_{4}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}\\ &\qquad \because p_{3}=p_{2}, p_{4}=p_{1} \\ \frac{1500}{T_{4}}&=(6)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}}=(6)^{0.285}=1.666 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{4} &=\frac{1500}{1.666}=900.36 \mathrm{K} \\ &\approx 900 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

me:2011:q48.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 48
me:2011:q48.question:
In an experimental set-up, air flows between two stations P and Q adiabatically. The direction of flow depends on the pressure and temperature conditions maintained at P and Q. The conditions at station P are 150kPa and 350K. The temperature at station Q is 300K.
The following are the properties and relations pertaining to air:
Specific heat at constant pressure, $C_{p}$= 1.005kJ/kgK;
Specific heat at constant volume, $C_{v}$= 0.718kJ/kgK;
Characteristic gas constant, R=0.287kJ/kgK
Enthalpy, h=$C_{p}T$
Internal energy, u=$C_{v}T$

If the air has to flow from station P to station Q, the maximum possible value of pressure in kPa at station Q is close to

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} c_{p} &=1.005 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ c_{v} &=0.718 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ R &=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \gamma &=\frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}=\frac{1.005}{0.718}=1.4 \end{aligned}$$ For adiabatic process P-Q, $$\begin{aligned} \frac{T_{Q}}{T_{P}} &=\left(\frac{p_{Q}}{p_{P}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}} \\ \frac{300}{350} &=\left(\frac{p_{Q}}{150}\right)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}}=\left(\frac{p_{Q}}{150}\right)^{0.285} \\ \text{or}\qquad \frac{p_{Q}}{150} &=\left(\frac{300}{350}\right)^{3.5}\\ \frac{p_{Q}}{150}&=0.583\\ \text{or}\qquad p_{Q}&=87.45 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2011:q49.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 49
me:2011:q49.question:
In an experimental set-up, air flows between two stations P and Q adiabatically. The direction of flow depends on the pressure and temperature conditions maintained at P and Q. The conditions at station P are 150kPa and 350K. The temperature at station Q is 300K.
The following are the properties and relations pertaining to air:
Specific heat at constant pressure, $C_{p}$= 1.005kJ/kgK;
Specific heat at constant volume, $C_{v}$= 0.718kJ/kgK;
Characteristic gas constant, R=0.287kJ/kgK
Enthalpy, h=$C_{p}T$
Internal energy, u=$C_{v}T$

If the pressure at station Q is 50kPa, the change in entropy ($s_{Q}-s_{P}$) in kJ/kgK is

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown:
If $p_{Q}=50 \mathrm{kPa}$

Change in entropy,

$$\begin{aligned} s_{Q}-s_{P} &=c_{p} \ln \frac{T_{Q}}{T_{P}}-R \ln \frac{p_{Q}}{p_{P}} \\ &=1.005 \ln \frac{300}{350}-0.287 \ln \frac{50}{150} \\ &=1.005(-0.1541)-0.287(-1.098) \\ &=-0.1548+0.3151=0.160 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2011:q52.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 52
me:2011:q52.question:
A triangular-shaped cantilever beam of uniform-thickness is shown in the figure. The Young's modulus of the material of the beam is E. A concentrated load P is applied at the free end of the beam.


The area moment of inertia about the neutral axis of a cross-section at a distance x measured from the free end is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: Let, b = width of the base of triangle ABD = BD t = thickness of conilever beam From the similar triangle $\Delta ABC$ or $\Delta AFE$ $$\begin{aligned} \frac{b/2}{l}&=\frac{h}{x} \\ h&=\frac{bx}{2l} \end{aligned}$$ For a rectangular cross section, $$\begin{aligned} I&=\frac{2ht^3}{12}\\&=2 \times \frac{bx}{2l} \times \frac{t^3}{12} \\ I&=\frac{bxt^3}{12l} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2011:q53.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 53
me:2011:q53.question:
A triangular-shaped cantilever beam of uniform-thickness is shown in the figure. The Young's modulus of the material of the beam is E. A concentrated load P is applied at the free end of the beam.


The maximum deflection of the beam is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown:
Using the Double-Integration method to find out the deflection, given by

$$\begin{aligned} EI\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 y}{\mathrm{d} x^2}=-M&=-(-Px)\\ E\frac{bxt^3}{12l}\times\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 y}{\mathrm{d} x^2}&=Px\\ \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 y}{\mathrm{d} x^2}&=\frac{12Pl}{Ebt^3} \end{aligned}$$

On integrating, we get

$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=\frac{12Plx}{Ebt^3}+C_1 \;\;\;...(i)$

We know that, at  $x=l;\;\;\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=0$

$0=\frac{12Pl^2}{Ebt^3}+C_1$

$C_1=-\frac{12Pl^2}{Ebt^3}$

Integrating (i), we get

$y=\frac{12Pl}{Ebt^3}\times\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{12Pl^2}{Ebt^3} x+C_2$

At  $x=l;\;\;y=0$

$0=\frac{12Pl}{Ebt^3}\times\frac{l^2}{2}-\frac{12Pl^2}{Ebt^3} l+C_2$

$C_2=-\frac{6Pl^3}{Ebt^3}+\frac{12Pl^3}{Ebt^3}$

$C_2=\frac{6Pl^3}{Ebt^3}$

Hence, we have

$y=\frac{6Plx^2}{Ebt^3}-\frac{12Pl^2x}{Ebt^3} +\frac{6Pl^3}{Ebt^3}$

The maximum deflection will occur at x=0 , So

$y=0-0 +\frac{6Pl^3}{Ebt^3}$

$y=\frac{6Pl^3}{Ebt^3}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

me:2011:q54.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 54
me:2011:q54.question:
The temperature and pressure of air in a large reservoir are 400K and 3 bar respectively. A converging-diverging nozzle of exit area 0.005$m^{2}$ is fitted to the wall of the reservoir as shown in the figure. The static pressure of air at the exit section for isentropic flow through the nozzle is 50kPa. The characteristic gas constant and the ratio of specific heats of air are 0.287kJ/kgK and 1.4 respectively.


The density of air in $kg/m^{3}$ at the nozzle exit is

primary.subtopicLabel: First Law, Heat, Work and Energy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - First Law, Heat, Work and Energy
detailed_solution.markdown:
Density of air in $\left(\mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}\right)$ at nozzle exit is

$\frac{p_{1}}{\rho_{1}^{\gamma}}=\frac{p_{2}}{\rho_{2}^{\gamma}}$

where $\rho=$ density

$$\begin{array}{l} \rho_{2}=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{\gamma}} \rho_{1} \\ =\left(\frac{50}{300}\right)^{1 / 1.4} \times \frac{3 \times 10^{5}}{0.287 \times 1000 \times 400} \\ =0.727 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2011:q55.title: GATE ME 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 55
me:2011:q55.question:
The temperature and pressure of air in a large reservoir are 400K and 3 bar respectively. A converging-diverging nozzle of exit area 0.005$m^{2}$ is fitted to the wall of the reservoir as shown in the figure. The static pressure of air at the exit section for isentropic flow through the nozzle is 50kPa. The characteristic gas constant and the ratio of specific heats of air are 0.287kJ/kgK and 1.4 respectively.


The mass flow rate of air through the nozzle in kg/s is

primary.subtopicLabel: First Law, Heat, Work and Energy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - First Law, Heat, Work and Energy
detailed_solution.markdown:
Mass flow rate of air through nozzle

= mass entering nozzle

= mass exit from nozzle

$$\begin{aligned} m &=\rho_{i} A_{i} V_{i}=\rho_{e} A_{e} V_{e} \\ \text { where } & i=\text { inlet } \\ e &=\text { exit } \\ \rho &=\text { density } \\ A &=\text { Area } \\ V &=\text { velocity } \\ p &=\rho R T \\ m &=\frac{A_{e} V_{e} p_{e}}{R T_{e}}\\ \text{Given }R&=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ p_{e}&=50 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}$$

For isentropic process

$$\begin{array}{l} \left(\frac{T_{e}}{T_{i}}\right)=\left(\frac{p_{e}}{p_{i}}\right)^{\gamma-1 / \gamma} \\ \frac{T_{e}}{400}=\left(\frac{50}{500}\right)^{0.4 / 1.4}\\ \text{or}\quad T_{e}=239.73 \mathrm{K} \end{array}$$

Mass flow rate,

$m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times V_{e}}{0.287 \times 239.73} \qquad \cdots(1)$

Using steady flow energy equation

$$\begin{aligned} h_{i}+\frac{V_{i}^{2}}{2}+q&=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2}+w\\ \text{where }\quad V_{i}&=0 \\ q&=0 \quad \text{adiabatic flow}\\ w &=0 \\ \therefore \quad h_{i} &=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2} \end{aligned}$$

On units balancing, we get

$$\begin{aligned} h_{i} &=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000} \\ \text{or}\quad h_{i}-h_{e} &=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000}\\ c_{p}\left(T_{i}-T_{e}\right)&=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000}\\ 1 \times(400-239.73)&=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000} \\ V_{e}&=567.57 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

From Eq. (1), we get

$m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times 567.57}{0.287 \times 239.73}$

$=2.06 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.
